options: A straight path going on forever in both directions
A straight path with two endpoints
questions.explanation: A line is a straight path extending forever in both directions with no endpoints.
questions.misconception: The path with two endpoints is a segment, and the one with a single arrowhead is a ray — a line has arrowheads at both ends.

questions.prompt: What do the arrowheads on a line show?
questions.explanation: Arrowheads mean the path continues endlessly in that direction.
questions.misconception: Arrowheads are about the line never ending, not speed or straightness — a straight mark without arrowheads could be a segment.

questions.prompt: A line passes through points A and B. How can you name it?
questions.explanation: A line is named by two points on it — line AB.
questions.misconception: Segment AB has endpoints, ray AB has one endpoint, and angles use three points — a line just takes two points on it.

questions.prompt: What do you get if you stop a line at one end?
questions.explanation: Stopping a line at one end leaves a ray — one endpoint, one arrowhead.
questions.misconception: Stopping BOTH ends makes a segment; stopping just one end makes a ray, and the line itself has no ends to stop.

questions.explanation: A line has no thickness at all — the drawn stroke is only its symbol.
questions.misconception: The visible stroke has width for us to see it, but the true line is infinitely thin — width is not part of the definition.
